definition: Delineating organs, tumors, or lesions in medical scans such as MRI and CT.
details: Delineating organs, tumors, or lesions in medical scans such as MRI and CT. U-Net and its variants dominate, enabling quantitative diagnosis and treatment planning.

explainer.lead: Medical image segmentation delineates organs, tumours or lesions in scans such as MRI and CT. It matters because it enables quantitative diagnosis and treatment planning.

tiers.eli5: It is the process of drawing the outline around a tumour or organ on a scan so a doctor can see exactly where it is and how big it is.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build segmentation models dominated by U-Net and its variants to produce the outlines. A pitfall is that the output feeds diagnosis and planning, so delineation errors carry clinical consequences.
tiers.paperLevel: The task assigns a label to each pixel or voxel of the scan; U-Net and its variants are the dominant architectures. No formal formula or error bound is given.

explainer.example: A CT scan is passed through a U-Net variant that labels the tumour region for volume measurement before treatment planning.
